## Warnings

- Step 5: self-review mode: Claude subagent review complete
- The diff widens the grandfathered complexity ratchet baseline, which G-Enf-2 says must only shrink.

- Deviation. `python/complexity-baseline.json` raises two existing `close_priors_main` rows: C901 `metric` 12 -> 13 and PLR0912 `metric` 14 -> 15. G-Enf-2 requires a graduated-defect baseline to be grandfathered so it "only shrinks," warns that "widening the baseline ... silently re-admits the defect and defeats the ratchet," and records "Deviate when: n/a." Neither bumped row records a `reason` for the higher metric (both keep `added_at: legacy`, `history: []`), and G-Enf-2 asks every baseline row to carry a reason (G-Py-11). The check in `lint_complexity_baseline.py` fails on `live_metric > baseline_metric`, so raising the recorded metric is what re-admits the higher complexity under the grandfather cover.

- Mitigating context tied to the same diff: the growth adds no new grandfathered identity (the `close_priors_main` rows pre-exist), and it traces to a required integrity branch, the new `_issue_state_closed` post-close re-read added to `close_priors_main` in `python/larch/issue/audit_runs.py`, whose `if not _issue_state_closed(...): ...; continue` adds one branch in each metric dimension. The increase is therefore visible in the same diff rather than a silent re-admission. The residual deviation is that the baseline was raised rather than held or drained, with no per-row reason recorded for the bump; holding the metric flat (for example by extracting the loop body) would have kept the ratchet shrinking.

- The rest of the diff conforms. The post-close and post-label re-verifications in `audit_runs.py`, `combine_issues.py`, and `oos_filer.py` implement G-Py-8 and G-Ext-2 with narrow, named exception handling (G-Py-4) and frozen-dataclass returns (G-Py-1); the new `RECONCILE_STATUS_*` and `*_POSTCONDITION_UNVERIFIED` `Final` constants in `config.py`, consumed by `ship_recovery.py`, follow G-Cfg-1 while keeping the reconcile stdout byte-identical (G-Wire-1, pinned by a new test); `assessment_kind.py` routes fence detection through the shared `plan_grammar.balanced_fence_line_indices` and `is_fence_marker` helpers per G-Md-3, behind a reason-annotated function-level import that keeps `larch.core` off `larch.design` at import time (G-Py-12, G-Py-11); and the `CodexGateSignal` `Literal` with its `Final` members replaces the duplicated inline signal strings across both constructing call sites in `_auth.py` and `_launch_failure.py` (G-Py-3, G-Wire-3), co-located with the `CodexGateDetail` type in `_types.py` alongside the module's existing cross-module constants.
